subject: Lyric Health - dedicated commit fit + GPU headroom proposal
body:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Huang <sarah.huang@lyrichhealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lyric Health - dedicated commit fit + GPU headroom proposal

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I started a quick draft of the sizing approach so your procurement and engineering teams have something concrete to react to. The key open items I need from you to lock numbers (if you can confirm in-reply):

- Peak concurrent requests during business hours (typical and worst-case minutes)
- Average input + expected output token count per request (or a sample distribution)
- Target P95 latency SLO for text completions (ms) and for the embedding/rerank paths if applicable
- Whether you want a strict dedicated SLA (reserved GPUs) vs. a burst-capable commit (reserved + burst)

I sketched two sizing scenarios below based on the product profile you described on the call (mostly chat completions, 80% short summaries (avg 60 tokens out), 20% longer reports (avg 650 tokens out)). These are conservative assumptions — happy to tune after you share the token distribution CSV.

Scenario A — conservative commit (steady-state + 1.8x headroom)
- Expected peak token/sec requirement (observed peak pattern): 1,600 tokens/sec
- Model candidate: rw-13b-quant (8-bit friendly profile we discussed)
- Per-GPU sustained throughput (13B quantized) estimate: ~340 tokens/sec per GPU (measured on our 80GB A100 equivalent under continuous load)
- GPUs required raw = ceil(1600 / 340) = 5 GPUs -> round to 8 GPU slab for allocation unit
- Apply headroom factor 1.8 -> 8 * 1.8 = 14.4 -> recommend 16 GPUs reserved (2 x 8-GPU slabs)
- Expected P95 latency impact: with autoscaling + batching tuned to maintain p95 < 450ms for avg requests (short outputs will be well under 300ms).

Scenario B — aggressive (peak safety, caching + batching opt-in)
- Effective token/sec after prefix caching and KV reuse (estimated) = 1,200 tokens/sec
- Per-GPU throughput (with batching optimizations) = ~380 tokens/sec
- GPUs required raw = ceil(1200 / 380) = 4 GPUs -> allocate 8-GPU slab
- Add burst reserve slab for microbursts -> +8 GPUs reserved for instant burst -> total 16 GPUs reserved but cheaper burst plan possible

Notes / tradeoffs:
- Headroom: we recommend a minimum 2x headroom cushion for first 90 days to cover unforeseen traffic patterns and onboarding variability. That recommendation is reflected above as the 1.8x multiplier in Scenario A and explicit burst slab in B.
- Latency SLO mapping: smaller batch sizes reduce latency but increase GPU cost; we can target p95 <= 300ms by enabling prefix caching on frequent prompts and limiting the batch window to <10ms for short requests.
- Fallback plan: if commit budget is constrained, we propose a mixed-route policy: primary reserved 8-GPU slab with automatic routing to a lower-cost quantized variant or hosted fallback during spikes. This keeps user-facing availability but changes model fidelity in extreme events.

Attached: I asked Sarah on the call to send a sample token histogram — once I have that CSV I will re-run the slab math and attach a spreadsheet with the exact per-minute headroom curves.

Would you and procurement like me to convert Scenario A into a committed quote for counter-signing?

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the clear outline. Attached you'll find the token_profile CSV you asked for (aggregated by hour for last 30 days). A few clarifications from our side:

- Typical business-hours peak (M-F, 10:00–15:00 PT): ~1,400 tokens/sec average, with short bursts up to ~2,600 tokens/sec lasting 2–5 minutes when clinicians batch uploads.
- Avg request sizes: short summaries 55–75 tokens output (median 60), long reports 600–750 tokens output (median 650). Input prompts average ~30 tokens.
- Critical latency: P95 < 400ms for chat flows. For batch report generation we accept p95 up to 1,500ms.
- Compliance: must be private deployment with VPC peering and log retention for 90 days.

Tom from procurement is looped for contracting; we would prefer a committed reserved plan for predictability.

Sarah
Director of Product | Lyric Health
sarah.huang@lyrichhealth.ai
Attachment: lyric_token_profile.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Lyric Health - initial sizing notes

Priyom / Marissa —

Thanks Sarah for the CSV (cc'd here). Quick internal calc and recommendations based on the data (high level):

1) Baseline throughput requirement (sustained during business peak): use 1,400 tokens/sec as baseline; plan for 2,600 tok/s short burst.
2) Model choice: recommend rw-13b-4bit (best ops tradeoff for latency and cost). Measured med-sized instance throughput: ~360 tok/s per 80GB A100 equivalent under mixed request sizes with our batching profile.

Sizing arithmetic:
- Sustained GPUs needed = ceil(1400 / 360) = 4 -> allocate as 8-GPU slab unit to simplify ops.
- Burst headroom (to cover 2,600 tok/s) = additional ceil((2600-1400) / 360) = 4 GPUs -> 1 more 8-GPU slab for burst capacity.
- Recommended reserved commit: 8 GPUs (one slab) + 1 burst-capable slab (8 GPUs) for short duration spikes. This gives deterministic cost for procurement while delivering the 2.6k tok/s spikes through burst policy.

Latency mapping (p95): with one reserved slab + burst slab available, p95 for short chat flows should hit ~320–380ms if we enable prefix caching and client-side prompt shaping. If Lyric requires sub-300ms p95, we should push to 16 reserved GPUs (2 slabs) to collapse tail latency under heavy burst patterns.

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling cooldowns: set short (30–45s) cooldown for burst slab attach/detach, and track warm KV cache hit ratio in the first 2 weeks.
- Quantization/variants: offer a slightly faster 13B quant variant for latency-critical endpoints; fallback to standard quantized model for noncritical.

I'll prepare a workbook with minute-level headroom curves and cost delta for 8 vs 16 reserved GPU scenarios.

- Karthik
Director, Deployment Engineering | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Lyric Health - dedicated commit fit + GPU headroom proposal (proposal attached)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Appended the recommended commercial-ready proposal based on the preferred reserved + burst model (attached spreadsheet: gpu-slab-sizing.xlsx). High-level ask and recommend:

- Commit: 1 x 8-GPU slab reserved (guarantees 1,400 tok/s steady state)
- Burst: 1 x 8-GPU slab on burst policy (covers 2,600 tok/s 3–5 minute spikes)
- Optional upgrade: move to 2 x 8-GPU reserved (16 GPUs) if Lyric wants guaranteed p95 < 300ms for all interactive flows.
- Compliance notes: Private deployment + VPC peering supported; will include log retention config for 90 days in the SOW.

Next steps:
1) If procurement is happy, I can create a draft order form and SOW with the above commit and compliance addendum.
2) We’ll run a 2-week on-ramp with monitoring dashboards and a traffic replay test (we'll need a sanitized sample load from your infra team).
3) Post-on-ramp we’ll review actual KV cache hit rates and adjust the commit if traffic shape differs materially.

Tom — can procurement confirm preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. annual reserve)? Happy to hop on a 30-min call to finalize wording.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
